Bullet in the Head (1990)

R16Violence

Following a trio of gangsters (played by Tony Leung, Jacky Cheung, and Waise Lee) who decide to hide out from a murder rap in Hong Kong by taking a smuggling job in Vietnam just as the war is heating up in 1967. Almost immediately, the magnitude of their mistake becomes clear as they find themselves in the middle of guerrilla raids, terror campaigns, and clandestine activities by various foreign agents using the chaos to make a quick buck. "Director John Woo draws liberally from the trove of Vietnam War movies, staging epic battles in villages with overt cues to Apocalypse Now and mirroring The Deer Hunter’s structure of slow psychological unraveling among friends." - Slant Magazine COME EARLY! Doors 6:30pm, pre-show 7pm

Dead Calm (1989) Sam Neill Tribute

MViolence, offensive language & sex scenes

Phillip Noyce’s excellent psychological thriller Dead Calm, produced by Mad Max’s George Miller. An adaptation of Charles Williams’ novel of the same name - starring Sam Neill and Nicole Kidman as a married couple sailing off the Australian coast trying to forget the tragic death of their son. The couple encounter a man (Billy Zane) drifting out to sea, and attempt to help him, only to realise too late that he’s mad as a cut snake. The film was a huge critical success and won a number of awards in Australia. COME EARLY! Doors 6:30pm, pre-show 7pm

Death in Brunswick (1990) Sam Neill Tribute

MViolence & offensive language

A riotous rollercoaster of murder and mayhem set in multicultural inner Melbourne, this hit Australian comedy-thriller stars Sam Neill as Carl, a fortyish no-hoper whose takes a job as a cook in a seedy nightclub to escape his cantankerous mother. A flirtation with fetching barmaid Sophie (Zoe Carides) - who is engaged to the nightclub owner - lands Carl on the wrong side of a viscious bouncer; but when attacked by his drug-dealing Turkish kitchenhand, Carl inflicts a grievous form of self-defence that sparks a deepening gangland feud. Best mate Dave (John Clarke) is soon employed as Carl's protector - and gravedigger - as a band of cutthroats block Carl's path to his bartending sweetheart. "As fresh today as it was when it was made." COME EARLY! Doors 6:30pm, pre-show 7pm

Stories About My Body (2026) Director Q&A

TBC

We had so much fun at the World Premiere, we can't wait to bring you this special Q&A presentation. Created and performed by Morgana O'Reilly (The White Lotus) and co-directed with her husband and real-life birth partner, 2025 BAFTA nominee Peter Salmon (After The Party), Stories About My Body blends nudity, heart-swelling honesty and real birth footage into a stand-up comedy special like no other - intimate, fearless and unexpectedly profound. In a tiny theatre in Aotearoa, New Zealand, four teenage stagehands work tirelessly to help Morgana tell the stories that shaped her - from her own teenagehood in 1998, to working foot-fetish parties in New York City, to falling in love and later birthing her babies in a Melbourne living room. By turns vulnerable and riotously funny, she moves from lamenting her chins to marvelling at her cellular functions, using her body as the living template for every tale she tells. COME EARLY! Doors 5:30pm, pre-show 6pm, FEATURE STARTS 6:30pm Sharp! Q&A with Morgana O'Reilly directly afterwards.

The Fly (1986) 40th Anniversary

R16Violence & sex scenes

David Cronenberg's The Fly is that absolute rarity of the '80s: a film that is at once a pure, personal expression and a superbly successful commercial enterprise. David Cronenberg directs this meditation on obsession and power, creating a pitch perfect mad scientist story. When an experiment goes horrifically wrong, scientist Seth Brundle begins to experience a metamorphosis that threatens to overtake his humanity. Cronenberg handles Brundle's transformation into a giant fly masterfully, utilising creature effects that still make audiences sick to their stomachs thirty something years later. Truly one of the better examples of the modern monster movie. As a remake, The Fly transcends the original, taking it in new directions and exploring its underutilised potential.

The Sandlot Kids (1993)

PGCoarse language

If you grew up in the '90s, you know that they just don't make movies like they used to. The Sandlot Kids is one of the most beloved and quotable coming-of-age films that everyone in the family will enjoy. Certainly the sight of nine kids playing ball instead of Nintendo on a sunny day will draw a nostalgic sigh from any parent. In the summer of 1962, a new kid in town is taken under the wing of a young baseball prodigy and his rowdy team, resulting in many adventures. As the gang learns to work as a team off the field, the movie never loses its quick pace or its sense of fun. Old baseball wisdom: The best teams win with strong fundamentals. So do the best movies, an this is one of them! COME EARLY! Doors 3pm, pre-show 3:30pm
